name: types

types.name: AgenticConfig
types.description:
AgenticConfig is the configuration for the agentic workstation sensor.
 The daemon receives events from coding-agent hooks (PostToolUse,
 SubagentStart, etc.) via a Unix socket, batches them, and publishes
 to EventBus. From there, Aegis ingests the events for topology
 visualization and forensics.

fields.name: flush_interval_ms
fields.description: flush_interval_ms is the max time between event flushes to EventBus. Default: 5000.

fields.name: batch_size
fields.description: batch_size is the max events per flush. Default: 100.

fields.name: max_event_payload_bytes
fields.description:
max_event_payload_bytes caps how much of each tool input/output is
 stored per event. Larger payloads are truncated. Default: 32768 (32KB).

fields.name: file_pattern_excludelist
fields.description:
file_pattern_excludelist is a set of glob patterns for files to
 exclude from tracking. Example: ["*.lock", "node_modules/**", ".git/**"].

fields.name: spool_max_bytes
fields.description:
spool_max_bytes is the maximum spool file size in bytes. When the spool
 reaches this limit, new events are dropped until the backlog drains.
 Default: 524288000 (500MB).

types.name: Config
types.description:
Config is the per-profile configuration for cavalierctl.
 Loaded from all YAML files in ~/.cavalierctl/config/ and merged.
 Splitting connection and key into separate files (config.yaml + key.yaml)
 allows chmod 400 on the key file.

fields.name: connection
fields.description:
connection is the gRPC connection configuration.
 Used by the identity manager for token exchange with gateway.
 Contains endpoints, private_key, and trusted_cas.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is the single configuration type for all services.

 Bootstrap fields (endpoints, instance_id, private_key, trusted_cas) are loaded
 from YAML at boot and used to connect to the cluster.

 Runtime fields (ping_interval_ms, rebalance_interval_ms, listen_address,
 max_request_size, request_timeout_seconds, logger, shutdown_timeout_seconds)
 are delivered by the cluster via ServiceConfigState and can change at any time.

 TLS certificates are obtained automatically by the servicemanager via X509Mint
 after token exchange — they are not part of the config.

fields.name: endpoints
fields.description:
Cluster endpoints. Set in bootstrap file; can be updated at runtime
 via ServiceConfigState to add/remove endpoints dynamically.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id uniquely identifies this running instance/replica.
 Used for leader elections on boundaries with (spec.leader) = true.
 If empty, a random ID is generated at client creation time.

fields.name: private_key
fields.description:
private_key is used to mint throwaway bootstrap JWTs for the
 token exchange flow. The kid is in private_key.id;
 identity (subject/audience) comes from the delegate looked up
 by TokenExchanger using the matching kid.
 If absent, cloud-native authentication is attempted.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: ping_interval_ms
fields.description:
ping_interval_ms controls how often each endpoint is pinged for latency measurement.
 Default: 5000 (5 seconds)

fields.name: rebalance_interval_ms
fields.description:
rebalance_interval_ms controls how often the active connection is re-evaluated
 based on latency. Default: 10000 (10 seconds)

fields.name: listen_address
fields.description: listen_address is the bind address for the gRPC server. Default port 8443.

fields.name: max_request_size
fields.description:
max_request_size is the maximum request size in bytes.
 Must be greater than 0. Default: 10MB (10485760 bytes)

fields.name: request_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
request_timeout_seconds is the timeout for client requests.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: logger
fields.description:
logger configures the logger for the service.
 Controls log format (JSON/console), level, output paths, and more.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
shutdown_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
shutdown_timeout_seconds is the maximum time (in seconds) to wait for graceful
 shutdown after SIGTERM before forcing immediate shutdown.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description:
trusted_cas is the list of CA certificates trusted for TLS verification
 when connecting to cluster endpoints. If empty, system root CAs are used.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: format
fields.description: format is the default output format.

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: JSON format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_YAML
enum_values.description: YAML format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_MULTI_YAML
enum_values.description: Multi YAML format (e.g. ---)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TEXT
enum_values.description: Plain text format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_ENV_VAR
enum_values.description: Environment variable format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_PROTO_WIRE
enum_values.description: Protobuf wire format (binary)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TOML
enum_values.description: TOML format

types.name: CPSubsystemConfig
types.description:
CPSubsystemConfig configures the consensus-based strong consistency subsystem.
 Used for distributed locks, atomic counters, and leader election.
 Requires an odd number of members (minimum 3) for Raft quorum.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description:
enabled controls whether the CP subsystem is active.
 Must be enabled for distributed locks (Lock service) to work.

fields.name: cp_member_count
fields.description:
cp_member_count is the number of cluster members that participate in
 the CP (consensus protocol) group. Must be odd and >= 3.
 Only these members vote in Raft elections; others are observers.

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is the maximum time a CP session can be inactive
 before it is closed and its resources (locks, etc.) are released.

fields.name: session_heartbeat_interval_seconds
fields.description:
session_heartbeat_interval_seconds is the interval for CP session heartbeats.
 Must be less than session_timeout_seconds.

fields.name: missing_cp_member_auto_removal_seconds
fields.description:
missing_cp_member_auto_removal_seconds is how long to wait before automatically
 removing a missing CP member from the group. Set to 0 to disable auto-removal.

types.name: FullDumpHeader
types.description:
FullDumpHeader is the header written at the start of a full dump file.
 Legacy format: followed by individual RedoLogEntry records.

types.name: NetworkConfig
types.description: NetworkConfig configures cluster networking behavior.

fields.name: connect_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
connect_timeout_seconds is the maximum time to wait when connecting to a cluster member.
 Default: 5 seconds.

fields.name: heartbeat_interval_seconds
fields.description:
heartbeat_interval_seconds is the interval between heartbeat messages sent to cluster members.
 Used to detect failed nodes.

fields.name: heartbeat_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
heartbeat_timeout_seconds is the time after which a member is considered unreachable
 if no heartbeat is received. Must be greater than heartbeat_interval_seconds.

types.name: PersistenceDump
types.description:
PersistenceDump is a full snapshot of all registered IMaps.
 Written as a single length-prefixed record in dump files.

message.name: PersistenceEntry
message.description:
PersistenceEntry is a typed mutation entry for redo logs and full dumps.
 Replaces the former KitchenSink oneof envelope with google.protobuf.Any
 so that any proto message can be persisted without code generation.

types.name: RateLimitConfig
types.description:
RateLimitConfig configures rate limiting for unary read RPCs to detect polling.
 Two categories are tracked independently:
 - polling_rate: unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives (Watch/Subscribe)
 - unary_rate: unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives

fields.name: polling_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives.

fields.name: unary_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives.

 Legacy format: value stored as opaque bytes, requires a parser to deserialize.

enums.name: OpType

enums.name: ConsistencyType
enums.description: ConsistencyType identifies the consistency model for a redo log entry.

types.name: AgenticCodeEventBus
types.description:
AgenticCodeEventBus holds the event topic for all coding-agent sensor data.
 Sensor daemons (blueclaude, etc.) publish SensorEvents here; Aegis
 subscribes for workstation-side observability. The sensor_type field on
 each event identifies the originating agent.

fields.name: event_stream
fields.description: event_stream is the EventBus topic for sensor events.

message.name: SensorEvent
message.description:
SensorEvent is the top-level event published to EventBus.
 Each event represents one hook firing in one coding-agent session.

fields.name: issuer

fields.name: event_id

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is when the hook fired (wall clock on the workstation).

fields.name: event_type
fields.description: event_type classifies this event.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TASK_COMPLETED

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_COMPACT

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_PROMPT

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_STOP

types.name: TokenMintRequest
types.description:
TokenMintRequest is the unified input for the TokenMint RPC.
 Covers both direct exchange (caller presents credentials) and delegation
 (broker mints on behalf of another principal).

 Direct exchange: input_token or cloud_proof authenticates the caller.
   Subject is derived from the credentials. Profiles are resolved from
   the Delegate's authorized_profiles.

 Delegation: caller authenticates via header (service token). Subject,
   profiles, and claims are specified explicitly. Kernel verifies the
   caller is authorized to delegate.

fields.name: input_token
fields.description: input_token is a JWT to validate (delegate cred_pair JWT or refresh token).

fields.name: cloud_proof
fields.description:
cloud_proof is a cloud-native identity proof (AWS STS, GCP, Azure).
 Used instead of input_token for cloud-native auth.

message.name: CloudIdentityProof
message.description:
CloudIdentityProof carries a cloud-native identity assertion.
 Exactly one of presigned_request or identity_token must be set,
 determined by the cloud vendor.

fields.name: vendor
fields.description: vendor identifies the cloud provider that issued this proof.

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AWS
enum_values.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AZURE
enum_values.description: Microsoft Azure

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_GCP
enum_values.description: Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ORACLE
enum_values.description: Oracle Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ALIBABA
enum_values.description: Alibaba Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_IBM
enum_values.description: IBM Cloud

fields.name: presigned_request
fields.description:
presigned_request is used for AWS: a signed STS GetCallerIdentity
 request that the server executes to verify the caller's IAM identity.
 The request has a short TTL to prevent replay.

message.name: PresignedHttpRequest
message.description:
PresignedHttpRequest carries a pre-signed HTTP request that the server
 executes on behalf of the caller. For AWS, this is a SigV4-signed
 STS GetCallerIdentity request.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the HTTP method (e.g. "POST").

fields.name: url
fields.description: url is the full request URL including query parameters.

fields.name: headers
fields.description:
headers are the signed HTTP headers that must be forwarded verbatim.
 Keys are header names, values are header values.

fields.name: body
fields.description: body is the request body (e.g. "Action=GetCallerIdentity&Version=2011-06-15").

fields.name: identity_token
fields.description:
identity_token is used for GCP and Azure: a signed JWT or OAuth2
 token obtained from the cloud metadata service. The server validates
 it against the provider's public JWKS/OIDC endpoint.

fields.name: continuity_token
fields.description:
continuity_token is a non-expired refresh token proving instance continuity
 across restarts. Optional.

fields.name: aud
fields.description: aud is the target service for the issued token.

fields.name: exp
fields.description: exp is the desired expiry epoch (optional; 0 = use default, capped by server policy).

fields.name: token_purpose
fields.description: token_purpose selects refresh or access token semantics.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_REFRESH
enum_values.description: Refresh token — long-lived, used to obtain new access tokens.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_ACCESS
enum_values.description: Access token — short-lived, carries entitlements for a specific service.

fields.name: subject
fields.description:
subject is the token's sub claim. Empty = derive from credentials.
 Brokers set this explicitly when minting on behalf of another principal.

fields.name: claims
fields.description:
claims are custom claims to embed in the token (e.g., origin IDP claims,
 auth_type, azp). Standard JWT claims (sub, iss, aud, exp, iat, jti) are
 set by kernel and must not appear here.

fields.name: profiles
fields.description:
profiles are identity profile names to resolve into entitlements.
 Kernel resolves each profile via identity_profiles config to get concrete
 per-service RPC lists for the target service (aud).

types.name: TokenMintResponse
types.description:
TokenMintResponse is the response from the TokenMint RPC.
 Always contains an access token. On initial exchange (cred_pair or cloud
 bootstrap), also contains a refresh token so callers get both in one call.

fields.name: access_token
fields.description: access_token is the primary token — a signed JWT for the requested audience.

message.name: Token
message.description:
Token represents a JWT (JSON Web Token) with header, payload, and signature components.
 The token can be in either parsed form (header/payload maps) or encoded form (base64 string).

fields.name: header
fields.description: Header contains the JWT header claims (e.g., alg, typ, kid)

fields.name: payload
fields.description:
JWT payload claims stored as string values. Numeric claims (exp, iat, nbf)
 are stored as decimal string representations (e.g., "1742403600").

fields.name: signature
fields.description: Signature is the base64url-encoded signature

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the complete JWT in base64url format (header.payload.signature)

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.description:
refresh_token is only populated on initial exchange (bootstrap).
 Callers cache it and use it to obtain new access tokens later.

types.name: X509MintRequest
types.description:
X509MintRequest is the input for the X509Mint RPC.
 Authentication comes from the caller's bearer token — either in the
 Authorization header or in the input_token field (for gateway-mediated
 calls). The token's sub claim identifies the service; kernel creates a
 per-service intermediate CA and signs the certificate under it.

fields.name: aud
fields.description: aud is the intended audience / service name for the certificate.

fields.name: cert_request

message.name: X509CertRequest
message.description:
X509CertRequest represents a certificate signing request (CSR) for generating X.509 certificates.
 It contains the public key to be certified, validity period, key usage constraints,
 and issuer information needed to create a signed certificate.

fields.name: key
fields.description: Key is the public key to be certified

message.name: PublicKey
message.description:
PublicKey represents a public cryptographic key.
 The key is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block in PKIX format.
 Use NewProtoPublicKey() in Go or similar constructors in other languages to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM public key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: exp
fields.description: Exp is the expiration timestamp (Unix time) for the certificate

fields.name: metadata
fields.description: Metadata contains additional information about the certificate request

fields.name: key_usage
fields.description: KeyUsage specifies the intended cryptographic operations (e.g., "digitalSignature", "keyEncipherment")

enum_values.name: X509_KEY_USAGE_DIGITAL_SIGNATURE
enum_values.description: X509KeyUsageDigitalSignature indicates digital signature usage

enum_values.name: X509_KEY_USAGE_CONTENT_COMMITMENT
enum_values.description: X509KeyUsageContentCommitment indicates content commitment (non-repudiation)

enum_values.name: X509_KEY_USAGE_KEY_ENCIPHERMENT
enum_values.description: X509KeyUsageKeyEncipherment indicates key encipherment

enum_values.name: X509_KEY_USAGE_DATA_ENCIPHERMENT
enum_values.description: X509KeyUsageDataEncipherment indicates data encipherment

enum_values.name: X509_KEY_USAGE_KEY_AGREEMENT
enum_values.description: X509KeyUsageKeyAgreement indicates key agreement

enum_values.name: X509_KEY_USAGE_CERT_SIGN
enum_values.description: X509KeyUsageCertSign indicates certificate signing

enum_values.name: X509_KEY_USAGE_CRL_SIGN
enum_values.description: X509KeyUsageCRLSign indicates CRL signing

enum_values.name: X509_KEY_USAGE_ENCIPHER_ONLY
enum_values.description: X509KeyUsageEncipherOnly indicates encipher only

enum_values.name: X509_KEY_USAGE_DECIPHER_ONLY
enum_values.description: X509KeyUsageDecipherOnly indicates decipher only

fields.name: ext_key_usage
fields.description: ExtKeyUsage specifies extended key usage purposes for the certificate

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_ANY
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageAny indicates any extended key usage

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_SERVER_AUTH
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageServerAuth indicates TLS server authentication

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_CLIENT_AUTH
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageClientAuth indicates TLS client authentication

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_CODE_SIGNING
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageCodeSigning indicates code signing

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_EMAIL_PROTECTION
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageEmailProtection indicates email protection (S/MIME)

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_IPSEC_END_SYSTEM
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageIPSECEndSystem indicates IPSEC end system

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_IPSEC_TUNNEL
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageIPSECTunnel indicates IPSEC tunnel

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_IPSEC_USER
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageIPSECUser indicates IPSEC user

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_TIME_STAMPING
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageTimeStamping indicates time stamping

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_OCSP_SIGNING
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageOCSPSigning indicates OCSP signing

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_MICROSOFT_SERVER_GATED_CRYPTO
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageMicrosoftServerGatedCrypto indicates Microsoft Server Gated Crypto

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_NETSCAPE_SERVER_GATED_CRYPTO
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageNetscapeServerGatedCrypto indicates Netscape Server Gated Crypto

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_MICROSOFT_COMMERCIAL_CODE_SIGNING
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageMicrosoftCommercialCodeSigning indicates Microsoft Commercial Code Signing

enum_values.name: X509_EXT_KEY_USAGE_MICROSOFT_KERNEL_CODE_SIGNING
enum_values.description: X509ExtKeyUsageMicrosoftKernelCodeSigning indicates Microsoft Kernel Code Signing

fields.name: issuer
fields.description: Issuer is the distinguished name (DN) of the certificate issuer

fields.name: is_ca
fields.description: is_ca marks this as a CA certificate (adds BasicConstraints CA:TRUE).

fields.name: path_len_constraint
fields.description:
path_len_constraint limits CA signing depth (-1 = unlimited, 0 = leaf-only).
 Only meaningful when is_ca is true.

fields.name: dns_names
fields.description: dns_names adds Subject Alternative Name DNS entries to the certificate.

fields.name: uri_sans
fields.description: uri_sans adds Subject Alternative Name URI entries (e.g. SPIFFE IDs).

fields.name: input_token
fields.description:
input_token is the caller's service token (JWT). When gateway mediates
 the X509Mint call, the token is passed in the request body instead of
 the Authorization header. Matches TokenMintRequest's pattern.

types.name: AccountingMethod
types.description:
AccountingMethod identifies which RPC an event relates to.
 Only one field will be set — the rest default to 0 (UNSPECIFIED)
 and are not encoded by proto3, so there is no overhead.

types.name: EntitlementProfile
types.description:
EntitlementProfile defines a named set of entitlements for user authorization.
 OPA profiles_policy returns zero or more profile names; oauth resolves
 those names to concrete per-service RPC entitlements at token exchange time.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is the profile name (e.g. "user", "admin", "reader").

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts this profile to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = profile applies regardless of azp (backward compat / admin profiles).

enums.name: ServiceName
enums.description:
ServiceName provides type-safe service references for S2S authorization.
 Enum values use stable service IDs from explicit service declarations.

types.name: Services

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables OAuth2 authentication.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description:
scopes are the default OAuth2 scopes requested from all providers.
 If empty, defaults to ["openid", "profile", "email"].

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers is the list of OAuth2 identity provider configurations.

message.name: ProviderConfig
message.description: ProviderConfig configures a single OAuth2 identity provider.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Google", "Okta", "Microsoft").

fields.name: domains
fields.description:
domains maps email domains to this provider. When a user's email domain
 matches, they are routed to this IDP automatically.

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the OpenID Connect issuer URL.
 Used for .well-known/openid-configuration auto-discovery.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret.

fields.name: authorization_endpoint
fields.description: authorization_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered authorization URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: token_endpoint
fields.description: token_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered token URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: end_session_endpoint
fields.description: end_session_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered logout URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: scopes overrides the default scopes for this provider.

fields.name: nonce_expire_seconds
fields.description:
nonce_expire_seconds is how long OAuth2 nonces/state remain valid.
 Nonces prevent replay attacks in the authorization code flow.
 Minimum: 1 second. Maximum: 86400 (24 hours). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: jwk_refetch_interval_seconds
fields.description:
jwk_refetch_interval_seconds is the minimum interval between JWKS fetches
 from the same external IDP. Prevents excessive outbound requests.
 Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: profiles_policy
fields.description:
profiles_policy is the OPA policy for determining user entitlement profiles
 at token exchange time. Contains a filesystem.Directory bundle of .rego files.
 The policy's entry_point rule receives {claims: {<IDP claims>}} and must
 return {profiles: [string]}. Profile names are resolved to concrete
 entitlements via entitlement_profiles in kernel config.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: health_poll_interval_seconds
fields.description: How often to refresh health state (seconds). Default 5.

fields.name: enable_http
fields.description: Enable HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_http3
fields.description: Enable HTTP/3 listener (QUIC/UDP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_grpc
fields.description: Enable gRPC listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: tcp_listener
fields.description: TCP listener for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and gRPC. Default port 8443.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port

constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol

fields.name: quic_listener
fields.description: QUIC/UDP listener for HTTP/3. Default port 8443.

fields.name: lets_encrypt_email
fields.description:
lets_encrypt_email is the email address for Let's Encrypt account
 registration and certificate expiration notifications.
 If empty, letsencrypt will use "admin@<fqdn>".
 NOTES: needs email assertion

fields.name: http_listener
fields.description:
http_listener is the bind address for the HTTP server used for ACME HTTP-01
 challenge responses. Must be reachable on port 80 from the internet.
 Default port 80.

fields.name: renewal_check_interval_seconds
fields.description:
renewal_check_interval_seconds is how often to check if the certificate
 needs renewal (seconds). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: fqdn

 a Let's Encrypt certificate.

fields.name: anthropic_api_key
fields.description: anthropic_api_key is the API key for calling the Anthropic Claude API.

fields.name: model
fields.description:
model is the Claude model to use (e.g. "claude-sonnet-4-20250514").
 Default: "claude-sonnet-4-20250514".

fields.name: max_retries
fields.description:
max_retries is the maximum number of validation retry attempts
 before giving up on constructing the type. Default: 3.

fields.name: session_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
session_ttl_seconds is how long idle sessions are kept before expiry.
 Default: 3600 (1 hour).

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is the service-level configuration for dgraph.
 Node mode is determined by the NODE_MODE env var, not by this config.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is the role assigned to this node.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_ZERO
enum_values.description: Zero: cluster management, shard assignment, leader election.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_ALPHA
enum_values.description: Alpha: data storage, serves GraphQL/DQL queries.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_COMBINED
enum_values.description: Combined: runs both Zero and Alpha in a single container (dev only).

fields.name: zero_count
fields.description:
zero_count is the expected number of Zero nodes in the cluster.
 Zeros use this to form the Raft quorum. Default: 1.

fields.name: replicas
fields.description:
replicas is the number of Alpha replicas per data shard group.
 Used by Zero nodes.

fields.name: alpha_count
fields.description: alpha_count is the expected number of Alpha nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: event_retention_hours
fields.description:
event_retention_hours is how long observed tokens and conversation events
 are kept before pruning. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: max_graph_nodes
fields.description:
max_graph_nodes caps the number of entities returned in a single
 topology snapshot. Default: 5000.

fields.name: stale_entity_seconds
fields.description:
stale_entity_seconds is how long after the last observation an entity
 is considered stale and grayed out in the UI. Default: 300 (5 min).

fields.name: max_tool_call_payload_bytes
fields.description:
max_tool_call_payload_bytes caps how much of each tool call's input/output
 is stored. Larger payloads are truncated. Default: 65536 (64KB).

fields.name: simulation_profiles
fields.description: simulation_profiles maps profile names to simulation configurations.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config for the event-bus service. Stored in kernel via grpc_config.
 At boot, eventbus connects to kernel to fetch this config, then merges
 with env vars (env takes precedence via PROTO_CONFIG_* env var mappings).

fields.name: node_role
fields.description: node_role determines the embedded Kafka (KRaft) process role.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED: runs both broker and controller in one process.
 Simplest deployment for small clusters (3-5 nodes).

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER: data-only node. Stores partitions, serves producers
 and consumers. Scales horizontally.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER: metadata quorum only. Runs the KRaft consensus
 protocol for leader election and partition assignment.
 Deploy an odd number (3 or 5) for quorum.

fields.name: data_dir
fields.description: data_dir is the Kafka log/data directory.
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_DIR)

fields.name: default_retention_hours
fields.description: default_retention_hours for new topics. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: default_partitions
fields.description: default_partitions for new topics. Default: 6.

fields.name: default_replication_factor
fields.description: default_replication_factor for new topics. Default: 3.

fields.name: controller_count
fields.description: controller_count is the expected number of Controller nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: broker_count
fields.description: broker_count is the expected number of Broker nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: broker_port
fields.description: broker_port is the Kafka broker listener port.

fields.name: controller_port
fields.description: controller_port is the KRaft controller listener port.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: node_id is the unique KRaft node identifier for this instance.

fields.name: cluster_seed
fields.description: cluster_seed is a stable string used to deterministically derive the KRaft cluster UUID.

fields.name: state_refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: state_refresh_interval_seconds controls how often this node re-registers in EventbusState.

fields.name: hot_window_hours
fields.description:
hot_window_hours is the default hot cache retention window.
 Data older than this is evicted from HZ (still in Cassandra). Default: 3.

fields.name: reheat_ttl_minutes
fields.description:
reheat_ttl_minutes is the TTL for re-heated cold data pulled back
 into a separate HZ map. Shorter than the primary hot window so
 historical data ages independently. Default: 30.

fields.name: warm_retention_days
fields.description:
warm_retention_days is how long data lives in Cassandra before
 aging out to Iceberg. Default: 30.

fields.name: archive_compaction_hours
fields.description: archive_compaction_hours is how often Iceberg compaction runs. Default: 24.

fields.name: cache_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
cache_ttl_seconds is the default TTL for cached query results
 in the dedicated HZ query cache map. Default: 60.

fields.name: time_mask_seconds
fields.description:
time_mask_seconds is the default time parameter quantization
 resolution for query result caching. Queries within the same masked
 window share cache entries. Default: 60.

fields.name: max_fan_out
fields.description: max_fan_out is the max concurrent store queries per request. Default: 4.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the ClickHouse materialized view retention. Default: 90.

fields.name: batch_size
fields.description: batch_size is the max rows per insert batch. Default: 10000.

fields.name: flush_interval_ms
fields.description: flush_interval_ms is the max time between flushes. Default: 1000.

fields.name: keeper_count
fields.description: keeper_count is the expected number of Keeper nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: data_count
fields.description: data_count is the expected number of Data nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is the role assigned to this node.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_KEEPER
enum_values.description: Keeper: consensus/coordination (replaces ZooKeeper).

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_DATA
enum_values.description: Data: data storage, serves queries over HTTPS.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_COMBINED
enum_values.description: Combined: runs both Keeper and Data in a single container (dev only).

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is how long an unauthenticated bidi session
 waits for token delivery before timing out.
 Minimum: 30 seconds. Maximum: 600 (10 minutes). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for long-lived refresh
 tokens issued to CLI clients. Longer than browser sessions because
 laptops may be offline for extended periods.
 Minimum: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 2592000 (30 days). Default: 604800 (7 days).

fields.name: auto_refresh_before_seconds
fields.description:
auto_refresh_before_seconds is how far before token expiry the service
 proactively refreshes tokens for connected daemon clients.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

 kind of message), promote it to a typed event. Diagnostics are a migration
 path, not a permanent solution.

fields.name: stack_trace

types.name: Event
types.description:
Event is the top-level envelope for all typed events. It carries common
 context (source, identity, request tracing) and a typed payload.

 This is what gets published to EventBus, spooled for guaranteed delivery,
 and indexed by consumers.

fields.name: root_certs
fields.description:
RootCerts is a list of X.509 certificates to use as root CAs for verifying server certificates.
 If empty, the system's default root CAs will be used.
 Use this to trust custom or internal certificate authorities.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: client_cert
fields.description:
ClientCert is an X.509 certificate chain with private key for client authentication.
 Use this when the server requires mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication.
 chain[0] is the leaf cert, key must be set for mTLS.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: timeout_seconds
fields.description:
TimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds for the entire HTTP request/response cycle.
 This includes connection time, request writing, server processing, and response reading.
 A value of 0 means no timeout (wait indefinitely).
 Recommended: Set a reasonable timeout (e.g., 30 seconds) to prevent hanging requests.

fields.name: max_idle_conns
fields.description:
MaxIdleConns controls the maximum number of idle (keep-alive) connections across all hosts.
 A value of 0 means no limit. Default is typically 100 if not specified.

fields.name: max_idle_conns_per_host
fields.description:
MaxIdleConnsPerHost controls the maximum number of idle (keep-alive) connections per host.
 A value of 0 means use the default (typically 2). Increase for high-throughput scenarios.

fields.name: idle_conn_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
IdleConnTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds an idle connection will remain
 in the connection pool before being closed. A value of 0 means no limit.

fields.name: tls_handshake_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
TlsHandshakeTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds to wait for a TLS handshake.
 A value of 0 means no timeout. Recommended: 10 seconds.

fields.name: expect_continue_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
ExpectContinueTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds to wait for a server's
 first response headers after fully writing the request headers if the request has
 "Expect: 100-continue" header. A value of 0 means no timeout.

fields.name: response_header_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
ResponseHeaderTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds to wait for a server's
 response headers after fully writing the request (including body, if any).
 A value of 0 means no timeout.

fields.name: retry_config
fields.description:
RetryConfig configures retry behavior for HTTP requests.
 If not specified, default retry configuration will be used (3 retries, exponential backoff).

message.name: RetryConfig
message.description:
RetryConfig configures retry behavior for HTTP requests with exponential backoff.
 This configuration controls how failed requests are retried, including which errors
 and status codes trigger retries, and the backoff timing between attempts.

fields.name: max_retries
fields.description:
MaxRetries is the maximum number of retry attempts after the initial request.
 A value of 0 means no retries (only the initial request is made).
 Default: 3

fields.name: initial_backoff_ms
fields.description:
InitialBackoffMs is the initial backoff duration in milliseconds before the first retry.
 This value is multiplied by BackoffMultiplier for each subsequent retry.
 Default: 100ms

fields.name: max_backoff_ms
fields.description:
MaxBackoffMs is the maximum backoff duration in milliseconds.
 The backoff will never exceed this value, even after many retries.
 Default: 5000ms (5 seconds)

fields.name: backoff_multiplier
fields.description:
BackoffMultiplier is the multiplier applied to the backoff duration after each retry.
 For exponential backoff, use values like 2.0 (doubles each time).
 For linear backoff, use 1.0 (stays constant).
 Default: 2.0

fields.name: retryable_status_codes
fields.description:
RetryableStatusCodes are HTTP status codes that should trigger a retry.
 Common retryable codes: 429 (Too Many Requests), 500, 502, 503, 504.
 If empty, defaults to [429, 500, 502, 503, 504].
 Network errors (connection failures, timeouts) are always retried regardless of this setting.

fields.name: disable_validation
fields.description:
DisableValidation controls whether HTTP client responses are validated after retrieval.
 If false (default), responses are validated using ValidateType(*type) after being retrieved.
 If true, validation is skipped and raw responses are returned without validation.
 WARNING: Disabling validation may allow invalid data to propagate through your system.

types.name: Jwk
types.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, Hazelcast computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

types.name: Lock
types.description:
Lock provides optimistic concurrency control for atomic state boundaries.
 Clients acquire a lock via GetLock, include it in mutations, and release via ReleaseLock.
 The server uses the counter to verify the client still holds the lock.

services.name: LockService
services.description: LockService manages distributed locks for atomic state operations.

types.name: LoggerConfig
types.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:

types.name: GraphTypeAnnotation
types.description:
GraphTypeAnnotation marks a proto message as a graph type for schema generation.
 Used by subscribe-gen to generate DQL schema and mutation handlers,
 and by bigdata-gen for graph store projections.

 Design decisions (D1, D2, D3 from the graph schema plan):

 D1: Annotations go on SOURCE messages (e.g. GraphEntity in aegis.proto),
 not on the consumer. The source messages are the authority on the data model.
 This follows the same pattern as service_state, topic, and subscribe —
 the annotation lives where the structure is defined.

 D2: Nested messages WITHOUT graph_type are serialized as JSON string
 predicates. Graph storage is for traversal (structural fields), not
 analytical queries on metadata. JSON storage avoids ~50 null predicates
 per entity, prevents schema churn, and allows incremental promotion.

 D3: xid_field controls the mutation strategy. When set, subscribe-gen
 generates NQuad upsert (query by xid, conditional update-or-insert).
 When empty, subscribe-gen generates JSON insert (append-only).
types.schema_json:
{
  "name": "GraphTypeAnnotation",
  "package": "spec",
  "description": "GraphTypeAnnotation marks a proto message as a graph type for schema generation.
 Used by subscribe-gen to generate DQL schema and mutation handlers,
 and by bigdata-gen for graph store projections.

 Design decisions (D1, D2, D3 from the graph schema plan):

 D1: Annotations go on SOURCE messages (e.g. GraphEntity in aegis.proto),
 not on the consumer. The source messages are the authority on the data model.
 This follows the same pattern as service_state, topic, and subscribe —
 the annotation lives where the structure is defined.

 D2: Nested messages WITHOUT graph_type are serialized as JSON string
 predicates. Graph storage is for traversal (structural fields), not
 analytical queries on metadata. JSON storage avoids ~50 null predicates
 per entity, prevents schema churn, and allows incremental promotion.

 D3: xid_field controls the mutation strategy. When set, subscribe-gen
 generates NQuad upsert (query by xid, conditional update-or-insert).
 When empty, subscribe-gen generates JSON insert (append-only).",
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "name",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "name is the graph type name (e.g. "Entity", "Edge")."
    },
    {
      "name": "xid_field",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "xid_field is the proto field used as the external ID for upserts.
 When set, subscribe-gen generates upsert mutations keyed on this field.
 When empty, subscribe-gen generates insert-only JSON mutations."
    }
  ]
}

enums.name: ConsistencyModel
enums.description:
ConsistencyModel defines how a boundary field's state is stored and replicated.

 Storage model:
   - UNSPECIFIED (default): serialized as part of the parent message, not a separate IMap.
   - ATOMIC: own Hazelcast IMap with synchronous backups and optimistic locking.
     Mutations require a Lock (map name = service+field path, counter must match).
   - CONVERGENT: own Hazelcast IMap with asynchronous replication.
     Mutations are lockless (last-writer-wins / append-only).
   - INHERITED: inherits the consistency model of the enclosing parent boundary.

 Rules:
   - All direct children of a state root must specify ATOMIC, CONVERGENT, or INHERITED.
   - Map name for each boundary = "service_name+field_name+...n" (path through the state tree).
   - Non-repeated boundaries are singletons (IMap key = "").
   - Repeated boundaries require an (spec.indexed) field as the IMap key
     (validated at build time).

services.name: TlsCertService
services.description:
TlsCertService provides automatic TLS certificate lifecycle management.
 Kernel implements the server side. Services with auto_tls: true open a
 bidi stream via the generated ServiceManager.

 Flow:
   1. Service sends Init (identifies itself) + Csr (public key)
   2. Kernel signs cert under service's intermediate CA, returns CertDelivery
   3. At half-life, kernel sends Renew
   4. Service generates new keypair, sends Csr
   5. Kernel signs, returns CertDelivery
   6. Repeat from 3

fields.name: hot_window_hours
fields.description:
hot_window_hours is the default hot cache retention window.
 Data older than this is evicted from HZ (still in Cassandra). Default: 3.

fields.name: reheat_ttl_minutes
fields.description:
reheat_ttl_minutes is the TTL for re-heated cold data pulled back
 into a separate HZ map. Shorter than the primary hot window so
 historical data ages independently. Default: 30.

fields.name: warm_retention_days
fields.description:
warm_retention_days is how long data lives in Cassandra before
 aging out to Iceberg. Default: 30.

fields.name: archive_compaction_hours
fields.description: archive_compaction_hours is how often Iceberg compaction runs. Default: 24.

fields.name: cache_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
cache_ttl_seconds is the default TTL for cached query results
 in the dedicated HZ query cache map. Default: 60.

fields.name: time_mask_seconds
fields.description:
time_mask_seconds is the default time parameter quantization
 resolution for query result caching. Queries within the same masked
 window share cache entries. Default: 60.

fields.name: max_fan_out
fields.description: max_fan_out is the max concurrent store queries per request. Default: 4.

SubscribeRequest
types.description:
SubscribeRequest is sent on the bidi stream to control replay.
 The first message establishes the session; subsequent messages adjust
 position, speed, pause state, or backpressure without closing the stream.

 Every field is applied as-is — the server replaces its current state
 with the full contents of each new SubscribeRequest. To change only
 the speed, the client re-sends the same seek + the new speed.

fields.name: consumer_group
fields.description:
Consumer group for offset tracking. Only read from the first message;
 ignored on subsequent resubscribes (consumer group is immutable per session).

fields.name: speed_multiplier
fields.description:
speed_multiplier controls replay pacing relative to original event timestamps.
 0 = max throughput (catch-up mode, no delay between events).
 1.0 = real-time (events delivered at the same rate they were produced).
 10.0 = 10x fast-forward.
 Can be changed mid-stream without seeking.

fields.name: pause
fields.description:
pause stops delivery without closing the stream or releasing the consumer.
 The server holds its position. Send pause=false (or a new seek) to resume.

fields.name: backpressure
fields.description: backpressure tells the server what to do when the client is slow.

enum_values.name: BACKPRESSURE_BUFFER
enum_values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_BUFFER: server buffers events until the client catches up.
 Default gRPC behaviour. Safe but risks unbounded memory if the client
 falls behind permanently.

enum_values.name: BACKPRESSURE_DROP_OLD
enum_values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_DROP_OLD: server skips ahead to the latest available offset,
 discarding events the client couldn't consume in time. The client sees
 a gap but never falls behind.

enum_values.name: BACKPRESSURE_SAMPLE
enum_values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_SAMPLE: server delivers every Nth event (N = sample_interval),
 dropping the rest. Useful for dashboards that need shape, not completeness.

fields.name: sample_interval
fields.description:
sample_interval: when backpressure=BACKPRESSURE_SAMPLE, deliver every
 Nth event and drop the rest. Ignored for other policies.

fields.name: partitions
fields.description:
partitions restricts consumption to specific partition IDs.
 Empty = subscribe to all partitions (default, uses consumer-group rebalancing).
 When set, uses manual assignment (no rebalancing).

rpcs.description:
Session is a bidirectional stream between cavalierctl and Fleetwood.
 The client sends a session_id, then waits for token delivery.
 Fleetwood holds the stream open until InstallToken is called with a
 matching session_id or the session times out.

InstallToken is called by the webapp after OAuth completes for a
 CLI-originated flow. The webapp provides the session_id (from the
 OAuth state) and the short-lived refresh token. Fleetwood exchanges
 the short-lived token (as a delegate) for a long-lived refresh token
 and delivers it to the matching bidi stream.

services.name: FleetwoodSessionService

 Auth is disabled (auth_disabled) because the client doesn't have a
 token yet — the whole point of this flow is to obtain one.

rpcs.description:
PublishEvents receives sensor events from users and forwards to EventBus.
 Identity is established by the caller's JWT — the SensorEvent.username
 field is untrusted metadata.

SubscribeEvents streams curated events scoped to the caller's JWT email.
 The server matches events by comparing the subscriber's email claim
 against the caller.email Kafka header stamped by EventBus on publish.

services.name: HeraldService
services.description:
HeraldService is the user-facing event gateway for coding-agent observability.

 Users publish sensor events to Herald, which forwards them to EventBus (S2S).
 Users subscribe through Herald, which scopes events to the subscriber's
 JWT email claim and applies a curated visibility policy.

 EventBus remains S2S-only infrastructure — Herald owns the user contract.

types.name: BootstrapConfig
types.description:
BootstrapConfig is the top-level configuration for a Kernel node.
 Kernel provides distributed state management with gRPC access
 and clustered storage. This configuration is read once at boot and is
 immutable for the lifetime of the process.

 The config oneof determines how the gRPC configuration (Config)
 is sourced: from a URL, or from a local file.
 Unlike BootstrapConfig, Config can be reloaded at any time.

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.description:
cluster_name is the logical name for this cluster.
 All nodes in the same cluster must use the same name.

fields.name: listener
fields.description: listener is the gRPC bind address for the Kernel server. Default port 5000.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: members
fields.description:
members is the list of cluster member addresses for discovery (e.g. host=10.0.0.1, port=9443).
 At least one member must be specified for the node to join the cluster.

fields.name: node_count
fields.description:
node_count is the expected number of nodes in the cluster.
 Used for partition planning and quorum calculations.
 Must be at least 1.

fields.name: partition_count
fields.description:
partition_count is the number of partitions to distribute data across.
 More partitions enable finer-grained distribution but increase metadata overhead.
 Default: 271 (prime number for better distribution).
 Must be greater than 0.

fields.name: network
fields.description: network configures cluster networking (timeouts, heartbeats, etc.).

message.name: NetworkConfig
message.description: NetworkConfig configures cluster networking behavior.

fields.name: connect_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
connect_timeout_seconds is the maximum time to wait when connecting to a cluster member.
 Default: 5 seconds.

fields.name: heartbeat_interval_seconds
fields.description:
heartbeat_interval_seconds is the interval between heartbeat messages sent to cluster members.
 Used to detect failed nodes.

fields.name: heartbeat_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
heartbeat_timeout_seconds is the time after which a member is considered unreachable
 if no heartbeat is received. Must be greater than heartbeat_interval_seconds.

fields.name: logger
fields.description: logger configures logging for the Kernel server.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
persistence_dir
fields.description:
persistence_dir is the directory where DB dumps and redo logs are stored.
 Default: "data/kernel".

fields.name: persistence_format
fields.description:
persistence_format configures the serialization format for redo logs and dumps.
 Default: OUTPUT_FORMAT_PROTO_WIRE (binary protobuf).

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: JSON format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_YAML
enum_values.description: YAML format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_MULTI_YAML
enum_values.description: Multi YAML format (e.g. ---)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TEXT
enum_values.description: Plain text format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_ENV_VAR
enum_values.description: Environment variable format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_PROTO_WIRE
enum_values.description: Protobuf wire format (binary)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TOML
enum_values.description: TOML format

types.name: Cluster
types.description:
============================================================================
 Cluster State (cluster diagnostics, health, and metrics)
 ============================================================================

 Cluster is a state root that exposes cluster diagnostics and
 operational metrics. A background publisher in each node periodically
 computes metrics from JVM/Hazelcast APIs and writes them to the maps.
 Tacplus auto-generates Get/Set/Watch RPCs for each boundary.

 PATTERNS TO ADDRESS LATER:

 1. Filtered queries: GetMapEntries needs key_prefix filter and limit.
    The auto-generated collection Get doesn't support ad-hoc filtering.
    Needs a hand-wrapped RPC or a new tacplus pattern for parameterized
    queries on collections.

 2. Transient point-in-time queries: ListLocks returns a snapshot of
    lock state that changes too rapidly to publish to maps. Needs a
    hand-wrapped RPC. Same applies to thread deadlock detection —
    better as on-demand than periodic.

 3. Publisher latency vs event-driven updates: Watch fires when maps
    update, but the publisher writes on a fixed interval. For membership
    changes, consider event-driven publishing (MembershipListener
    triggers immediate cluster_info/cluster_health write) alongside
    periodic publishing for metrics.
