fields.description: controller_port is the KRaft controller listener port.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: node_id is the unique KRaft node identifier for this instance.

fields.name: cluster_seed
fields.description: cluster_seed is a stable string used to deterministically derive the KRaft cluster UUID.

fields.name: state_refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: state_refresh_interval_seconds controls how often this node re-registers in EventbusState.

fields.name: hot_window_hours
fields.description:
hot_window_hours is the default hot cache retention window.
 Data older than this is evicted from HZ (still in Cassandra). Default: 3.

fields.name: reheat_ttl_minutes
fields.description:
reheat_ttl_minutes is the TTL for re-heated cold data pulled back
 into a separate HZ map. Shorter than the primary hot window so
 historical data ages independently. Default: 30.

fields.name: warm_retention_days
fields.description:
warm_retention_days is how long data lives in Cassandra before
 aging out to Iceberg. Default: 30.

fields.name: archive_compaction_hours
fields.description: archive_compaction_hours is how often Iceberg compaction runs. Default: 24.

fields.name: cache_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
cache_ttl_seconds is the default TTL for cached query results
 in the dedicated HZ query cache map. Default: 60.

fields.name: time_mask_seconds
fields.description:
time_mask_seconds is the default time parameter quantization
 resolution for query result caching. Queries within the same masked
 window share cache entries. Default: 60.

fields.name: max_fan_out
fields.description: max_fan_out is the max concurrent store queries per request. Default: 4.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the ClickHouse materialized view retention. Default: 90.

fields.name: batch_size
fields.description: batch_size is the max rows per insert batch. Default: 10000.

fields.name: flush_interval_ms
fields.description: flush_interval_ms is the max time between flushes. Default: 1000.

fields.name: keeper_count
fields.description: keeper_count is the expected number of Keeper nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: data_count
fields.description: data_count is the expected number of Data nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is the role assigned to this node.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_KEEPER
enum_values.description: Keeper: consensus/coordination (replaces ZooKeeper).

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_DATA
enum_values.description: Data: data storage, serves queries over HTTPS.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_COMBINED
enum_values.description: Combined: runs both Keeper and Data in a single container (dev only).

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is how long an unauthenticated bidi session
 waits for token delivery before timing out.
 Minimum: 30 seconds. Maximum: 600 (10 minutes). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for long-lived refresh
 tokens issued to CLI clients. Longer than browser sessions because
 laptops may be offline for extended periods.
 Minimum: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 2592000 (30 days). Default: 604800 (7 days).

fields.name: auto_refresh_before_seconds
fields.description:
auto_refresh_before_seconds is how far before token expiry the service
 proactively refreshes tokens for connected daemon clients.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: anthropic_api_key
fields.description: anthropic_api_key is the API key for authenticating with the Anthropic API.

fields.name: openai_api_key
fields.description: openai_api_key is the API key for proxying to the OpenAI API (cross-provider).

fields.name: api_token
fields.description:
api_token is the API token for authenticating with the GitHub API.
 Supports personal access tokens (classic and fine-grained), OAuth tokens,
 and GitHub App installation tokens.

fields.name: api_token
fields.description:
api_token is the API token for authenticating with the GitLab API.
 Supports personal access tokens, project access tokens, group access
 tokens, and OAuth tokens.

fields.name: openai_api_key
fields.description: openai_api_key is the API key for authenticating with the OpenAI API.

fields.name: anthropic_api_key
fields.description: anthropic_api_key is the API key for proxying to the Anthropic API (cross-provider).

fields.name: visible_event_types
fields.description:
visible_event_types restricts which event types are visible to users.
 Empty = all visible. Prevents leaking detection heuristics or internal
 policy details through the user-facing event stream.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_SESSION_START
enum_values.description: Session lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TOOL_USE
enum_values.description: Tool use (any tool: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Agent, etc.)

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_SUBAGENT_START
enum_values.description: Subagent lifecycle — agent spawned or finished.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TASK_COMPLETED
enum_values.description: Task lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_COMPACT
enum_values.description: Context management.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_PROMPT
enum_values.description: User prompt submitted.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_STOP
enum_values.description: Stop — agent finished responding.

fields.name: max_subscribers
fields.description: max_subscribers is the maximum number of concurrent subscriber connections.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is the service-level configuration for eventspy.

fields.name: key_rotation_interval_seconds
fields.description:
key_rotation_interval_seconds is how often the exchanger rotates
 its own signing keys. Default: 24 hours.

fields.name: default_token_expiry_seconds
fields.description:
default_token_expiry_seconds is the default lifetime for issued
 access tokens when the request does not specify an expiry. Default: 1 hour.

fields.name: delegates
fields.description:
delegates hold credentials for services that can request tokens.
 Each delegate identifies a service and its authorized target services.

message.name: Delegate
message.description:
Delegate holds credentials for a service or machine client that can request tokens.
 Each delegate is identified by name (becomes "sub" in issued tokens)
 and authenticates via a signed JWT (verified against cred_pairs) or cloud identity.

 Two authorization models (mutually exclusive):
   - S2S: authorized_services → wildcard entitlements per listed service
   - Profile-based: authorized_profiles → EntitlementProfile → per-service RPC lists
     Used for machine clients (formerly ApiKey) that need fine-grained access.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the delegate's identity (becomes sub in issued tokens).

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
Public keys for verifying the delegate's signed JWT.
 Repeated to allow rotation (old + new key during transition).

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, Hazelcast computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

message.name: CloudIdentityMatcher
message.description:
CloudIdentityMatcher configures which cloud identities a delegate accepts.
 The delegate proves identity using a CloudIdentityProof; this config
 tells kernel what to expect.

fields.name: vendor
fields.description: vendor identifies the cloud provider.

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AWS
enum_values.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AZURE
enum_values.description: Microsoft Azure

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_GCP
enum_values.description: Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ORACLE
enum_values.description: Oracle Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ALIBABA
enum_values.description: Alibaba Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_IBM
enum_values.description: IBM Cloud

fields.name: expected_identity
fields.description:
expected_identity is the cloud identity to match against.
 AWS: IAM role ARN. GCP: service account email. Azure: managed identity client ID.

fields.name: authorized_services
fields.description:
authorized_services lists services this delegate can request tokens for.
 Values are generated ServiceName enum entries matching service declarations.
 The delegate can always request a token for itself (sub=name).
 Use SERVICE_NAME_ANY to allow all services.

fields.name: authorized_profiles
fields.description:
authorized_profiles lists entitlement profiles this delegate may use.
 When set, TokenMint resolves these profiles to per-service RPC lists
 via entitlement_profiles in Config. Mutually exclusive with authorized_services:
 a delegate uses either S2S (authorized_services) or profile-based
 (authorized_profiles) authorization, not both.

fields.name: custom_claims
fields.description:
custom_claims are static key-value pairs added to every access token
 minted for this delegate. Useful for identity claims (e.g. email).
 Standard JWT claims (sub, iss, aud, exp, iat, azp, nbf, jti, typ, profiles)
 are reserved and will be skipped.

fields.name: ca_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
ca_cert_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for node CA certificates.
 Default: 31536000 (1 year). Node CA certs are regenerated on restart.

fields.name: entitlement_profiles
fields.description:
entitlement_profiles defines named sets of entitlements for user and machine
 authorization. OPA policy in OAuth returns profile names; kernel resolves
 those to concrete per-service RPC lists when OAuth calls MintToken.
 Also used by TokenMint to resolve Delegate.authorized_profiles for machine clients.

message.name: EntitlementProfile
message.description:
EntitlementProfile defines a named set of entitlements for user authorization.
 OPA profiles_policy returns zero or more profile names; oauth resolves
 those names to concrete per-service RPC entitlements at token exchange time.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is the profile name (e.g. "user", "admin", "reader").

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts this profile to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = profile applies regardless of azp (backward compat / admin profiles).

fields.name: access_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
access_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for user access tokens
 minted via MintToken. Default: 900 (15 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for user refresh tokens
 minted via MintToken. Default: 86400 (24 hours).

fields.name: trust_domain
fields.description:
trust_domain is the SPIFFE trust domain for this cluster.
 Used to construct SPIFFE IDs: spiffe://<trust_domain>/<azp>/<service>.
 Default: "cavalier".

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description:
fqdn is the fully qualified domain name for this cluster
 (e.g. "api.example.com"). Published to Identity state for
 services like letsencrypt. No default — must be set for production.
constraints: must be a fully qualified domain name

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the full issuer URL for tokens minted by this cluster.
 For local development, computed as https://<fqdn>:<port> (port omitted if 443).
 For production behind a load balancer, set explicitly (e.g. "https://api.example.com").

fields.name: tls_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
tls_cert_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for auto-TLS service certificates.
 Kernel sends a renewal request at half-life. Default: 86400 (24 hours).

fields.name: max_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
max_token_lifetime_seconds is the maximum lifetime kernel will allow for
 any minted token. Requests with exp beyond now + this value are rejected.
 Delegates control their own exp policy within this ceiling.
 Default: 2592000 (30 days).

fields.name: graph_registry
fields.description:
graph_registry contains metadata for all boundaries across all state roots.
 Published once at boot from the generated Registry. Keyed by qualified_name.
 Consumers use WatchGraphRegistry to discover all graphs in the system.

message.name: AdminGraphInfo
message.description:
AdminGraphInfo describes a single graph boundary in the system.
 Published once at boot from the generated Registry metadata.

fields.name: service_connections
fields.description:
service_connections tracks which microservices are connected and what
 graphs they are accessing. Published periodically by the security
 interceptor based on authenticated peer identity. Keyed by "service_id@node_id".

message.name: AdminServiceConnection
message.description:
AdminServiceConnection tracks a connected microservice's aggregate activity
 on a single node. Published periodically by the security interceptor.

fields.name: active_connections
fields.description: Connection counts

fields.name: total_rpcs
fields.description: RPC counts

fields.name: active_streams
fields.description: Streaming

fields.name: poll_count
fields.description: Polling detection

fields.name: per_method_counts
fields.description: Per-method detail

fields.name: accessed_graphs
fields.description: Per-graph detail

fields.name: peers
fields.description: Per-peer detail

message.name: AdminPeerActivity
message.description: AdminPeerActivity tracks activity from a single gRPC transport connection.

fields.name: connected_at_ms
fields.description: Timestamps

fields.name: rate_limited_count
fields.description: Rate limiting

fields.name: total_errors
fields.description: Errors

fields.name: latency
fields.description: Latency

message.name: AdminLatencyStats
message.description: AdminLatencyStats captures response time distribution (microseconds).

message.name: AdminMethodLatency
message.description: AdminMethodLatency pairs a method name with its latency distribution.

fields.name: bytes_received
fields.description: Payload sizes

message.name: AdminMethodPayload
message.description: AdminMethodPayload captures payload size statistics for a single method.

fields.name: per_graph_mutation_counts
fields.description: Mutation tracking

fields.name: queue_stats
fields.description:
queue_stats captures per-queue statistics (depth, offer/consume rates).
 Published per-queue per-node. Keyed by qualified_name.

message.name: AdminQueueStats
message.description: AdminQueueStats captures statistics for a queue or priority queue boundary.

fields.name: topic_stats
fields.description:
topic_stats captures per-topic statistics (publish rate, subscriber count).
 Published per-topic per-node. Keyed by qualified_name.

message.name: AdminTopicStats
message.description: AdminTopicStats captures statistics for a pub/sub topic boundary.

message.name: AdminTopicSubscriber
message.description: AdminTopicSubscriber tracks a single subscriber to a topic.

fields.name: watch_health
fields.description:
watch_health tracks active Watch streams and their consumer health.
 Published per-active-watch per-node. Keyed by watch_id.

message.name: AdminWatchHealth
message.description: AdminWatchHealth tracks the health of an active Watch stream.

fields.name: mutation_rates
fields.description:
mutation_rates captures per-boundary write throughput.
 Published per-boundary per-node. Keyed by qualified_name.

message.name: AdminMutationRate
message.description: AdminMutationRate captures write throughput for a single boundary.

types.name: CollectionQuery
Config
types.description:
Config is the gRPC configuration for Kernel.
 Unlike BootstrapConfig (read once at boot), Config can be reloaded at any time.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description: trusted_cas lists the trusted CA certificates for TLS verification.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: rate_limit
fields.description: rate_limit configures rate limiting for unary read RPCs to detect polling.

message.name: RateLimitConfig
message.description:
RateLimitConfig configures rate limiting for unary read RPCs to detect polling.
 Two categories are tracked independently:
 - polling_rate: unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives (Watch/Subscribe)
 - unary_rate: unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives

fields.name: polling_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives.

fields.name: unary_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives.

fields.name: configs
fields.description:
configs holds per-service configurations. On each config load,
 each entry is written to the corresponding service config state boundary.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables OAuth2 authentication.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description:
scopes are the default OAuth2 scopes requested from all providers.
 If empty, defaults to ["openid", "profile", "email"].

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers is the list of OAuth2 identity provider configurations.

message.name: ProviderConfig
message.description: ProviderConfig configures a single OAuth2 identity provider.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Google", "Okta", "Microsoft").

fields.name: domains
fields.description:
domains maps email domains to this provider. When a user's email domain
 matches, they are routed to this IDP automatically.

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the OpenID Connect issuer URL.
 Used for .well-known/openid-configuration auto-discovery.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret.

fields.name: authorization_endpoint
fields.description: authorization_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered authorization URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: token_endpoint
fields.description: token_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered token URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: end_session_endpoint
fields.description: end_session_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered logout URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: scopes overrides the default scopes for this provider.

fields.name: nonce_expire_seconds
fields.description:
nonce_expire_seconds is how long OAuth2 nonces/state remain valid.
 Nonces prevent replay attacks in the authorization code flow.
 Minimum: 1 second. Maximum: 86400 (24 hours). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: jwk_refetch_interval_seconds
fields.description:
jwk_refetch_interval_seconds is the minimum interval between JWKS fetches
 from the same external IDP. Prevents excessive outbound requests.
 Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: profiles_policy
fields.description:
profiles_policy is the OPA policy for determining user entitlement profiles
 at token exchange time. Contains a filesystem.Directory bundle of .rego files.
 The policy's entry_point rule receives {claims: {<IDP claims>}} and must
 return {profiles: [string]}. Profile names are resolved to concrete
 entitlements via entitlement_profiles in kernel config.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: health_poll_interval_seconds
fields.description: How often to refresh health state (seconds). Default 5.

fields.name: enable_http
fields.description: Enable HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_http3
fields.description: Enable HTTP/3 listener (QUIC/UDP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_grpc
fields.description: Enable gRPC listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: tcp_listener
fields.description: TCP listener for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and gRPC. Default port 8443.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: quic_listener
fields.description: QUIC/UDP listener for HTTP/3. Default port 8443.

fields.name: lets_encrypt_email
fields.description:
lets_encrypt_email is the email address for Let's Encrypt account
 registration and certificate expiration notifications.
 If empty, letsencrypt will use "admin@<fqdn>".
 NOTES: needs email assertion

fields.name: http_listener
fields.description:
http_listener is the bind address for the HTTP server used for ACME HTTP-01
 challenge responses. Must be reachable on port 80 from the internet.
 Default port 80.

fields.name: renewal_check_interval_seconds
fields.description:
renewal_check_interval_seconds is how often to check if the certificate
 needs renewal (seconds). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description:
fqdn is the fully qualified domain name for which to request
 a Let's Encrypt certificate.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is the service-level configuration for the MCP assist service.

fields.name: anthropic_api_key
fields.description: anthropic_api_key is the API key for calling the Anthropic Claude API.

fields.name: model
fields.description:
model is the Claude model to use (e.g. "claude-sonnet-4-20250514").
 Default: "claude-sonnet-4-20250514".

fields.name: max_retries
fields.description:
max_retries is the maximum number of validation retry attempts
 before giving up on constructing the type. Default: 3.

fields.name: session_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
session_ttl_seconds is how long idle sessions are kept before expiry.
 Default: 3600 (1 hour).

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is the service-level configuration for dgraph.
 Node mode is determined by the NODE_MODE env var, not by this config.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is the role assigned to this node.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_ZERO
enum_values.description: Zero: cluster management, shard assignment, leader election.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_ALPHA
enum_values.description: Alpha: data storage, serves GraphQL/DQL queries.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_COMBINED
enum_values.description: Combined: runs both Zero and Alpha in a single container (dev only).

fields.name: zero_count
fields.description:
zero_count is the expected number of Zero nodes in the cluster.
 Zeros use this to form the Raft quorum. Default: 1.

fields.name: replicas
fields.description:
replicas is the number of Alpha replicas per data shard group.
 Used by Zero nodes.

fields.name: alpha_count
fields.description: alpha_count is the expected number of Alpha nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: event_retention_hours
fields.description:
event_retention_hours is how long observed tokens and conversation events
 are kept before pruning. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: max_graph_nodes
fields.description:
max_graph_nodes caps the number of entities returned in a single
 topology snapshot. Default: 5000.

fields.name: stale_entity_seconds
fields.description:
stale_entity_seconds is how long after the last observation an entity
 is considered stale and grayed out in the UI. Default: 300 (5 min).

fields.name: max_tool_call_payload_bytes
fields.description:
max_tool_call_payload_bytes caps how much of each tool call's input/output
 is stored. Larger payloads are truncated. Default: 65536 (64KB).

fields.name: simulation_profiles
fields.description: simulation_profiles maps profile names to simulation configurations.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config for the event-bus service. Stored in kernel via grpc_config.
 At boot, eventbus connects to kernel to fetch this config, then merges
 with env vars (env takes precedence via PROTO_CONFIG_* env var mappings).

fields.name: node_role
fields.description: node_role determines the embedded Kafka (KRaft) process role.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED: runs both broker and controller in one process.
 Simplest deployment for small clusters (3-5 nodes).

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER: data-only node. Stores partitions, serves producers
 and consumers. Scales horizontally.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER

fields.name: data_dir

constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_DIR)

fields.name: default_retention_hours
fields.description: default_retention_hours for new topics. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: default_partitions
fields.description: default_partitions for new topics. Default: 6.

fields.name: default_replication_factor
fields.description: default_replication_factor for new topics. Default: 3.

fields.name: controller_count

fields.name: broker_count

fields.name: broker_port
fields.description: broker_port is the Kafka broker listener port.

fields.name: controller_port
fields.description: controller_port is the KRaft controller listener port.

fields.name: node_id

fields.name: cluster_seed
fields.description: cluster_seed is a stable string used to deterministically derive the KRaft cluster UUID.

fields.name: state_refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: state_refresh_interval_seconds controls how often this node re-registers in EventbusState.

fields.name: hot_window_hours
fields.description:
hot_window_hours is the default hot cache retention window.
 Data older than this is evicted from HZ (still in Cassandra). Default: 3.

fields.name: reheat_ttl_minutes
fields.description:
reheat_ttl_minutes is the TTL for re-heated cold data pulled back
 into a separate HZ map. Shorter than the primary hot window so
 historical data ages independently. Default: 30.

fields.name: warm_retention_days
fields.description:
warm_retention_days is how long data lives in Cassandra before
 aging out to Iceberg. Default: 30.

fields.name: archive_compaction_hours
fields.description: archive_compaction_hours is how often Iceberg compaction runs. Default: 24.

fields.name: cache_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
cache_ttl_seconds is the default TTL for cached query results
 in the dedicated HZ query cache map. Default: 60.

fields.name: time_mask_seconds
fields.description:
time_mask_seconds is the default time parameter quantization
 resolution for query result caching. Queries within the same masked
 window share cache entries. Default: 60.

fields.name: max_fan_out
fields.description: max_fan_out is the max concurrent store queries per request. Default: 4.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the ClickHouse materialized view retention. Default: 90.

fields.name: batch_size
fields.description: batch_size is the max rows per insert batch. Default: 10000.

fields.name: flush_interval_ms
fields.description: flush_interval_ms is the max time between flushes. Default: 1000.

fields.name: keeper_count
fields.description: keeper_count is the expected number of Keeper nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: data_count
fields.description: data_count is the expected number of Data nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is the role assigned to this node.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_KEEPER

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_DATA
enum_values.description: Data: data storage, serves queries over HTTPS.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_COMBINED
enum_values.description: Combined: runs both Keeper and Data in a single container (dev only).

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is how long an unauthenticated bidi session
 waits for token delivery before timing out.
 Minimum: 30 seconds. Maximum: 600 (10 minutes). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for long-lived refresh
 tokens issued to CLI clients. Longer than browser sessions because
 laptops may be offline for extended periods.
 Minimum: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 2592000 (30 days). Default: 604800 (7 days).

fields.name: auto_refresh_before_seconds
fields.description:
auto_refresh_before_seconds is how far before token expiry the service
 proactively refreshes tokens for connected daemon clients.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: key_rotation_interval_seconds
fields.description:
key_rotation_interval_seconds is how often the exchanger rotates
 its own signing keys. Default: 24 hours.

fields.name: default_token_expiry_seconds
fields.description:
default_token_expiry_seconds is the default lifetime for issued
 access tokens when the request does not specify an expiry. Default: 1 hour.

fields.name: delegates
fields.description:
delegates hold credentials for services that can request tokens.
 Each delegate identifies a service and its authorized target services.

message.name: Delegate
message.description:
Delegate holds credentials for a service or machine client that can request tokens.
 Each delegate is identified by name (becomes "sub" in issued tokens)
 and authenticates via a signed JWT (verified against cred_pairs) or cloud identity.

 Two authorization models (mutually exclusive):
   - S2S: authorized_services → wildcard entitlements per listed service
   - Profile-based: authorized_profiles → EntitlementProfile → per-service RPC lists
     Used for machine clients (formerly ApiKey) that need fine-grained access.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the delegate's identity (becomes sub in issued tokens).

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
Public keys for verifying the delegate's signed JWT.
 Repeated to allow rotation (old + new key during transition).

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, Hazelcast computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

message.name: CloudIdentityMatcher
message.description:
CloudIdentityMatcher configures which cloud identities a delegate accepts.
 The delegate proves identity using a CloudIdentityProof; this config
 tells kernel what to expect.

fields.name: vendor
fields.description: vendor identifies the cloud provider.

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AWS
enum_values.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AZURE
enum_values.description: Microsoft Azure

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_GCP
enum_values.description: Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ORACLE
enum_values.description: Oracle Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ALIBABA
enum_values.description: Alibaba Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_IBM
enum_values.description: IBM Cloud

fields.name: expected_identity
fields.description:
expected_identity is the cloud identity to match against.
 AWS: IAM role ARN. GCP: service account email. Azure: managed identity client ID.

fields.name: authorized_services
fields.description:
authorized_services lists services this delegate can request tokens for.
 Values are generated ServiceName enum entries matching service declarations.
 The delegate can always request a token for itself (sub=name).
 Use SERVICE_NAME_ANY to allow all services.

fields.name: authorized_profiles
fields.description:
authorized_profiles lists entitlement profiles this delegate may use.
 When set, TokenMint resolves these profiles to per-service RPC lists
 via entitlement_profiles in Config. Mutually exclusive with authorized_services:
 a delegate uses either S2S (authorized_services) or profile-based
 (authorized_profiles) authorization, not both.

fields.name: custom_claims
fields.description:
custom_claims are static key-value pairs added to every access token
 minted for this delegate. Useful for identity claims (e.g. email).
 Standard JWT claims (sub, iss, aud, exp, iat, azp, nbf, jti, typ, profiles)
 are reserved and will be skipped.

fields.name: ca_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
ca_cert_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for node CA certificates.
 Default: 31536000 (1 year). Node CA certs are regenerated on restart.

fields.name: entitlement_profiles
fields.description:
entitlement_profiles defines named sets of entitlements for user and machine
 authorization. OPA policy in OAuth returns profile names; kernel resolves
 those to concrete per-service RPC lists when OAuth calls MintToken.
 Also used by TokenMint to resolve Delegate.authorized_profiles for machine clients.

message.name: EntitlementProfile
message.description:
EntitlementProfile defines a named set of entitlements for user authorization.
 OPA profiles_policy returns zero or more profile names; oauth resolves
 those names to concrete per-service RPC entitlements at token exchange time.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is the profile name (e.g. "user", "admin", "reader").

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts this profile to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = profile applies regardless of azp (backward compat / admin profiles).

fields.name: access_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
access_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for user access tokens
 minted via MintToken. Default: 900 (15 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for user refresh tokens
 minted via MintToken. Default: 86400 (24 hours).

fields.name: trust_domain
fields.description:
trust_domain is the SPIFFE trust domain for this cluster.
 Used to construct SPIFFE IDs: spiffe://<trust_domain>/<azp>/<service>.
 Default: "cavalier".

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description:
fqdn is the fully qualified domain name for this cluster
 (e.g. "api.example.com"). Published to Identity state for
 services like letsencrypt. No default — must be set for production.
constraints: must be a fully qualified domain name

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the full issuer URL for tokens minted by this cluster.
 For local development, computed as https://<fqdn>:<port> (port omitted if 443).
 For production behind a load balancer, set explicitly (e.g. "https://api.example.com").

fields.name: tls_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
tls_cert_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for auto-TLS service certificates.
 Kernel sends a renewal request at half-life. Default: 86400 (24 hours).

fields.name: max_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
max_token_lifetime_seconds is the maximum lifetime kernel will allow for
 any minted token. Requests with exp beyond now + this value are rejected.
 Delegates control their own exp policy within this ceiling.
 Default: 2592000 (30 days).

types.name: Identity
types.description:
Identity holds the public verifying keys for kernel's token exchange service.
 Kernel is the sole token authority — all tokens (S2S, U2S, refresh) and
 X.509 certificates are signed by kernel's keys.

 Token exchange handles:
   1. Direct exchange: delegate presents cred_pair JWT or cloud proof → token/cert
   2. Delegation: broker (OAuth, K8S) authenticates via header, mints on behalf

 Access: RW for kernel, RO for any service that needs to verify tokens.

fields.name: verifying_keys
fields.description:
Verification keys — kernel's public keys, rotated periodically.
 Kernel holds the corresponding private keys internally.
 Used by SecurityInterceptor to validate tokens for cluster calls.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, Hazelcast computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description:
fqdn is the cluster's public hostname, published from Config on
 each config load. Services (e.g. letsencrypt) watch this to discover
 the cluster FQDN without needing it in their own config.

message.name: IdentityFqdn
message.description:
IdentityFqdn wraps the cluster's FQDN for publication as a singleton

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, Hazelcast computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

rpcs.description:
TokenMint mints a signed JWT token. Handles both direct credential
 exchange and delegated minting from brokers (OAuth, K8S brokers).

X509Mint signs an X.509 certificate under a per-service intermediate CA.
 Authentication via bearer token in the Authorization header or
 input_token in the request body (for gateway-mediated calls).

 On each call, kernel:
   1. Extracts the service name from the token's sub claim.
   2. Gets or creates an intermediate CA for that service
      (signed by root CA, pathlen:0).
   3. Signs the caller-provided public key (cert_request.key)
      under the intermediate CA.
   4. Returns X509CertChain: leaf cert + intermediate CA cert in chain.

 The intermediate CA is unique per service, providing per-service
 trust isolation — only nodes of the same service verify each other.

services.name: KernelMintService
services.description:
MintService is kernel's identity authority — mints tokens and signs
 certificates. Kernel is the sole signing authority for the cluster.
 Hand-written implementation; tacplus generates client wrappers and server wiring.

 Gateway owns the public-facing MintService (OIDC discovery, JWKS, and
 REST endpoints) and delegates TokenMint/X509Mint to kernel via its
 direct kernel channel. This service is for S2S use only.

 Both RPCs handle direct exchange (caller presents credentials in the request)
 and delegation (broker authenticates via header, specifies subject/profiles).
 Kernel determines the mode from the request: if subject is set, it's delegation
 and the caller must be an authorized delegate implementation.

rpcs.description:
ListProviders returns the configured OAuth2 providers (public info only).
 The webapp calls this to render provider selection buttons.
 Convention: POST|GET /api/v1/oauth/ListProviders

Authorize initiates the OAuth2 authorization code flow.
 Creates a nonce/state in memory and returns the IDP redirect URL.
 The caller provides a callback_url for post-auth redirect.
 Convention: POST /api/v1/oauth/Authorize

Callback handles the OAuth2 authorization code callback from the IDP.
 If this instance originated the flow (has the nonce in memory), it
 completes the exchange directly. Otherwise, it publishes the callback
 to the callback_relay topic for the originating instance to handle.
 Convention: POST /api/v1/oauth/Callback

Logout invalidates the session and optionally redirects to the IDP logout.
 Convention: POST /api/v1/oauth/Logout

# tacplus Registry

This file is embedded in `registry.json` and describes how to navigate it.

## Overview

This registry describes a tacplus-generated service mesh with:
- **866** message types across **54** packages
- **523** RPCs across **50** gRPC services
- **54** state boundaries

## Structure

The registry is a recursive `PackageNode` tree. Each node has:
- `name` — short package name
- `full_path` — slash-separated path from root
- `children` — sub-packages
- `types` — message type descriptors (`TypeInfo`)
- `rpcs` — RPC descriptors (`RpcInfo`)
- `boundaries` — state boundary descriptors (`BoundaryInfo`)

Navigate by traversing `children` to reach any package. The tree mirrors the proto package hierarchy.

## Self-Description

The `$schema` field points to `registry.schema.json` (JSON Schema format).
The type definitions under `libs/tacplus` describe this document's own structure:
`PackageNode`, `TypeInfo`, `FieldInfo`, `RpcInfo`, `BoundaryInfo`, `EnumValueInfo`, `StatePermEntry`.

## RPC Categories

Every RPC is classified by verb convention:
- **ACCESSOR** — read/observe operations (Get, Watch, Query, KeySet, Size, ContainsKey, List, Peek, Subscribe)
- **MUTATOR** — write/modify operations (Set, Put, Delete, Remove, Clear, Publish, Offer, Reload)
- **EXECUTOR** — action/command operations (Assist, Authenticate, Authorize, Evaluate, Exchange, etc.)

Per-service aggregate enum values (`ALL_ACCESSORS`, `ALL_MUTATORS`, `ALL_EXECUTORS`) are available for security policy rules.

## Security Metadata

Each `BoundaryInfo` carries:
- `state_perms` — which other state roots this service accesses (target + mode: RO/RW/WORM/CALL)
- `internal` — namespace isolation flag
- `boundary_callers` — which services can call this boundary cross-namespace
- `boundary_perms` — per-boundary access overrides

Each `RpcInfo` carries:
- `disable_auth` — whether authentication is bypassed
- `allowed_callers` — service-level caller restrictions
- `allow_user` — whether end-user tokens are accepted
- `category` — accessor/mutator/executor classification

# JBMC (Java Bounded Model Checker) Integration for tacplus

## Goal

Add Java formal verification using JBMC to complement Kani (Rust) verification. JBMC verifies our custom-generated `validate()` methods in `Helpers.java` and `Validation.java` — NOT the protobuf-generated code itself.

## Why JBMC, not OpenJML

OpenJML (ESC mode) was tried and fails catastrophically on protobuf-generated Java code. It crashes with `EmptyStackException` in `JmlAssertionAdder.visitTypeApply` when processing protobuf's complex generic type hierarchy (`GeneratedMessageV3<M>`, `Builder<M, B>`). This is an OpenJML bug with no workaround.

JBMC operates on **compiled bytecode** (.class files), not source. It never needs to parse protobuf's generic source — it just sees the compiled classes. This sidesteps the entire problem.

## What is JBMC

- Homepage: https://www.cprover.org/jbmc/
- Based on CBMC (C Bounded Model Checker), same family as Kani
- Performs bounded model checking on Java bytecode
- Verifies assertions, array bounds, null pointer safety, arithmetic overflow
- Works with standard `assert` statements — no special annotation language needed

## Architecture

### Data flow

```
Proto annotations (assert_max_size, assert_gt, assert_invariant, ...)
  → Java codegen emits validate() methods in Helpers.java / Validation.java
  → Java codegen emits JBMC proof harnesses in a separate Proof.java file
  → `tacplus verify` compiles the generated Java code (javac / mvn compile)
  → JBMC runs on compiled .class files containing proof harnesses
  → Results parsed into VerificationReport for verification-report.md
```

### Proof harness design

Generate a `Proof.java` class per proto file with static harness methods. Each harness:

1. Creates a message using its Builder with `Verifier.nondetInt()` / `Verifier.nondetString()` etc. for nondeterministic inputs
2. Constrains inputs with `org.cprover.CProver.assume()` based on proto annotations
3. Calls `validate()` and asserts it does not throw

Example generated harness:

```java
public class Proof {
    // JBMC harness: verify Token.validate() accepts all valid inputs
    public static void verify_token_validate() {
        Token.Builder builder = Token.newBuilder();

        // Nondeterministic inputs
        String header = org.cprover.CProver.nondetString();

        // Annotation-derived assumptions
        org.cprover.CProver.assume(header != null);
        org.cprover.CProver.assume(header.length() <= 16);

        builder.setHeader(header);
        Token msg = builder.build();

        // This should not throw for any input satisfying assumptions
        try {
            Helpers.validateToken(msg);
        } catch (ProtoException e) {
            assert false : "validate threw for valid input: " + e.getMessage();
        }
    }
}
```

### Key differences from Kani approach

| Aspect | Kani (Rust) | JBMC (Java) |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| Input generation | `kani::any()` on prost structs | `CProver.nondetX()` per field via Builder |
| Assumptions | `kani::assume(expr)` | `CProver.assume(expr)` |
| Assertions | `assert!(expr)` | `assert expr` |
| Operates on | Source (cargo build) | Bytecode (.class files) |
| Trait requirement | `Arbitrary` derive on prost types | None — uses Builders |
| Compilation | `cargo kani` | `javac` then `jbmc` |

The Builder pattern is the key insight: unlike Rust where we need `Arbitrary` on prost structs, Java protobuf Builders let us construct messages field-by-field with nondeterministic values. No special derives needed.

## Implementation steps

### 1. Install JBMC in the container

In `Dockerfile.base`, add JBMC installation. JBMC is distributed as part of CBMC:

```dockerfile
# JBMC (Java Bounded Model Checker)
RUN apt-get install -y cbmc
# or download from https://github.com/diffblue/cbmc/releases
```

Verify with: `jbmc --version`

### 2. Generate proof harnesses

Create a new file: `pkg/internal/java/types/proof.go`

This mirrors `pkg/internal/rust/types/proof.go` (the Kani harness generator). It should:

- For each message with provable annotations, generate a `verify_<message>_validate()` static method
- Use `org.cprover.CProver.nondetInt()`, `nondetString()`, etc. for nondeterministic field values
- Use `org.cprover.CProver.assume()` for annotation-derived preconditions
- Call the validate method and assert no exception

Field type mapping for nondeterministic values:
- `string` → `CProver.nondetString()` (but JBMC's string support is limited — may need `CProver.nondetInt()` for length + constructed string)
- `int32`, `sint32`, `sfixed32` → `CProver.nondetInt()`
- `int64`, `sint64`, `sfixed64` → `CProver.nondetLong()`
- `uint32`, `fixed32` → `CProver.nondetInt()` (constrain >= 0)
- `uint64`, `fixed64` → `CProver.nondetLong()` (constrain >= 0)
- `bool` → `CProver.nondetBoolean()`
- `float` → `CProver.nondetFloat()`
- `double` → `CProver.nondetDouble()`
- `bytes` → skip (JBMC doesn't handle ByteString well)
- `message` (nested) → recursively build with nondet values, or skip
- `repeated` / `map` → skip initially (complex for bounded model checking)

### 3. Add JBMC runner

Create: `pkg/verification/jbmc.go`

This mirrors `pkg/verification/kani.go`. Steps:

1. Find `Proof.java` files in the output directory
2. Compile them: `javac -cp <classpath> Proof.java` (classpath must include protobuf-java and the generated .class files)
3. Run JBMC: `jbmc --classpath <classpath> Proof --function Proof.verify_token_validate --unwind 10`
4. Parse JBMC output — it reports `VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL` or `VERIFICATION FAILED` with counterexample
5. Collect results into `VerificationHarness` structs

JBMC invocation per harness:
```bash
jbmc --classpath target/classes:protobuf-java.jar \
     Proof \
     --function Proof.verify_token_validate \
     --unwind 10 \
     --string-max-length 20
```

Key flags:
- `--unwind N` — loop unwinding bound (start with 10, increase if needed)
- `--string-max-length N` — bound on string length for analysis
- `--json-ui` — machine-readable JSON output (easier to parse)

### 4. Wire into verification.go

Add `"java"` case to the language switch in `pkg/verification/verification.go`:

```go
case "java":
    runner = runJbmc
```

### 5. Classpath resolution

The JBMC runner needs the Java classpath. For Maven projects:
- Generated classes: `target/classes/`
- Dependencies: parse `mvn dependency:build-classpath` output, or use `target/dependency/*.jar`

For Gradle projects:
- Generated classes: `build/classes/java/main/`
- Dependencies: parse `gradle dependencies` or use `build/libs/*.jar`

The existing `resolveJavaClassPath()` logic (from the deleted `openjml.go`) can be adapted.

### 6. Test plan

1. Build tacplus: `cd /Users/jody/workspace/services/tacplus && just`
2. Build kernel (Java): `cd /Users/jody/workspace/services/kernel && tacplus build --tag latest`
3. Verify: `cd /Users/jody/workspace/services/kernel && tacplus verify`
4. Check `verification-report.md` for JBMC results
5. Verify that harnesses with known-good annotations pass
6. Verify that a deliberately broken annotation (e.g., wrong bound) fails

## Caveats

- JBMC's string reasoning is limited. For string-heavy validations (email regex, FQDN, base64), the harness may need to skip those fields or use concrete test values instead of nondeterministic ones.
- Bounded model checking only proves correctness up to the unwind bound. This is still valuable — it catches bugs in validation logic — but it's not a full proof like deductive verification.
- JBMC may be slow on large messages with many fields. Consider generating harnesses only for messages with explicit annotations (same filter as Kani).
- The `org.cprover.CProver` class is provided by JBMC's runtime library, not a Maven dependency. The proof harness file needs this on the compile classpath.

## Files to create/modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `Dockerfile.base` | Install JBMC/CBMC |
| `pkg/internal/java/types/proof.go` | **New** — generate JBMC proof harnesses (Proof.java) |
| `pkg/internal/java/types/builder.go` | Call `writeJbmcHarnesses()` during generation |
| `pkg/verification/jbmc.go` | **New** — JBMC runner + output parser |
| `pkg/verification/verification.go` | Add `"java"` case dispatching to `runJbmc` |
| `cmd/verify/cmd.go` | Update help text to mention JBMC |

## Reference

- JBMC documentation: https://www.cprover.org/jbmc/
- CBMC releases: https://github.com/diffblue/cbmc/releases
- CProver API: the `org.cprover.CProver` class ships with JBMC
- Existing Kani implementation: `pkg/internal/rust/types/proof.go` and `pkg/verification/kani.go`

# Tacplus Registry Generation - Quick Reference Card

## The Big Picture
Tacplus generates **language-specific registry files** that expose complete metadata (types, boundaries, RPCs) across your entire microservice build.

---

## What Gets Generated

### Per Language
| Language | Registry File(s) | Location |
|----------|------------------|----------|
| **Go** | registry.go | `types/registry.go` + per-proto `types/services/*/registry.go` |
| **Java** | Registry.java | `types/Registry.java` |
| **Python** | registry.py | `sm/internal/state_clients/registry.py` |
| **TypeScript** | registry.ts | `types/registry.ts` |
| **Rust** | registry.rs | `types/registry.rs` |

---

## Registry Structure (3 Layers)

```
LAYER 1: ROOT REGISTRY (types/registry.go or types/Registry.java)
├─ Boundaries() - all boundaries across full build
├─ Types() - all type descriptors
├─ LookupType(fqn) - O(1) type lookup
└─ Services().ServiceName() - hierarchical navigation

LAYER 2: PROTO REGISTRY (types/services/<svc>/<pkg>/registry.go) [GO ONLY]
├─ TypeID enum - message identifiers
├─ RpcID enum - RPC method identifiers
├─ TypeName(id) / RpcName(id) - enum to string
└─ Types() - package-specific types

LAYER 3: STATE CLIENTS (sm/internal/state_clients/registry.go)
├─ Boundaries() - simple boundary list
└─ GetBoundary(service, boundary) - state access
```

---

## What's Exposed

### BoundaryInfo
```proto
message BoundaryInfo {
  ServiceName service          // Which service owns this
  string state_root             // e.g. "ClusterState"
  string boundary              // e.g. "ClusterInfo"
  ConsistencyModel consistency // atomic/convergent/etc
  bool persistence             // Is it persisted?
}
```

### TypeInfo
```proto
message TypeInfo {
  string fqn              // "kernel.ClusterState"
  string name             // "ClusterState"
  string package          // "kernel"
  string description      // Documentation
  string schema_json      // Full JSON schema (recursive)
  repeated FieldInfo fields
}
```

### FieldInfo
```proto
message FieldInfo {
  string name
  TypeKind type                    // message/enum/scalar
  bool required
  bool repeated
  repeated string constraints      // Validation rules
  TypeInfo message                 // Nested descriptor
  repeated EnumValueInfo enum_values
  string map_key_type / map_value_type
}
```

---

## Generator Flow (Command to Code)

```
$ tacplus build --src /path/to/protos --config tacplus.yaml

     ↓

cmd/build/cmd.go:runBuild()
     ↓
pkg/runner/runner.go:Build()
     ↓
    [Language-specific]
pkg/internal/go/types/generator.go:Generate()
     ↓
1. Copy protos + rewrite
2. Overlay libs protos
3. Run protoc
4. **generateRegistry()** ← THE KEY FUNCTION
   ├─ Parse service_state annotations
   ├─ Collect types via llmdesc.CollectRegistryTypes()
   ├─ Build TypeDescriptor for each (including schema JSON)
   ├─ Execute template (templates/go/types/registry.go.tmpl)
   └─ Output types/registry.go
5. Per-proto registries (Go: types/services/.../registry.go)
6. Inject TypeID/RpcID enums (pkg/internal/proto/registry_enums.go)
7. Service wrappers + HTTP clients
     ↓
Run post-gen hooks
```

---

## Key Source Files

### Proto Definitions
- `pkg/proto/libs/tacplus.proto` - BoundaryInfo, TypeInfo, RpcInfo, EnumValueInfo
- `pkg/proto/libs/spec.proto` - ConsistencyModel, TypeKind enums

### Templates
- `templates/go/types/registry.go.tmpl`
- `templates/java/types/registry.java.tmpl`
- `templates/python/types/registry.py.tmpl`

### Core Generator
- `pkg/internal/common/llmdesc/registry.go:CollectRegistryTypes()` - **Type collection algorithm**
- `pkg/internal/go/types/stateclient_gen.go:generateRegistry()` - **Go registry generation**
- `pkg/internal/java/types/statewrapper_gen.go:generateJavaRegistry()` - **Java registry generation**
- `pkg/internal/proto/registry_enums.go:InjectRegistryEnums()` - **TypeID/RpcID injection**

### Entry Points
- `cmd/build/cmd.go:runBuild()` - CLI entry
- `main.go` - tacplus executable

---

## tacplus.yaml Configuration

```yaml
language: go                              # go, java, typescript, python, rust
output-dir: tacplus                       # output subdirectory (required)
pkg: com.gitlab.myorg.myservice           # Canonical package name (Java-style reverse DNS)
states:                                   # State services to import
  - services/identity.IdentityState:rw    # Read-write
  - services/kernel.ClusterState:ro       # Read-only
grpc-servers:                                # gRPC services
  - services/identity.IdentityService
post-gen:                                 # Post-generation hooks
  - cmd: /bin/sh
    args: ["-c", "make generate"]
```

---

## Type Collection Algorithm

```
CollectRegistryTypes(allProtoFiles)
  1. Build index of all messages and enums
  2. For each proto file → For each message:
     a. Create FQN = package + "." + name
     b. Build TypeDescriptor recursively:
        - For each field: collect type, constraints
        - Nested messages: recurse and embed
        - Enums: collect all values
     c. Marshal to JSON schema
     d. Determine TypeDir (services vs libs)
     e. Append RegistryTypeInfo
  3. Sort by FQN (deterministic)
  4. Return []RegistryTypeInfo
```

---

## API Usage Examples

### Go
```go
// Root registry
boundaries := registry.Boundaries()
types := registry.Types()
info := registry.LookupType("kernel.ClusterState")

// Hierarchical
svcBoundaries := registry.Services().Kernel().Boundaries()
svcTypes := registry.Services().Identity().Types()

// Per-proto (Go only)
import "types/services/identity/identity"
name := identity.TypeName(identity.TypeID_TYPE_ID_CONFIG)
typeInfo := identity.TypeInfo(identity.TypeID_TYPE_ID_CONFIG)
```

### Java
```java
List<Tacplus.BoundaryInfo> all = Registry.boundaries();
Tacplus.BoundaryInfo b = Registry.lookupByShortName("services.kernel.ClusterState");
Tacplus.TypeInfo t = Registry.lookupType("kernel.ClusterState");
String path = Registry.servicePath(b);
Hazelcast.AdminGraphType gt = Registry.graphType(shortName);
```

### Python
```python
boundaries = registry.boundaries()
boundary = registry.get_boundary("services/snoopy", "TaskQueue")
```

---

## Generated Output Structure

```
service/tacplus/
├── registry/registry.go                  (State clients only)
├── proto/                                (Rewritten protos)
│   └── services/service/service.proto   (+ TypeID/RpcID enums)
├── types/                                (Language-specific generated)
│   ├── registry.go                       (✓ Go | Java)
│   ├── libs/
│   │   ├── generated/
│   │   │   ├── generated.pb.go          (ServiceName enum)
│   │   │   └── helpers.go               (LLM assist registry)
│   │   ├── tacplus/                     (Proto types)
│   │   └── spec/
│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── service1/package1/
│   │   │   ├── *.pb.go
│   │   │   ├── helpers.go
│   │   │   └── registry.go              (✓ Go only)
│   │   └── ...
│   └── ...
├── sm/
│   └── internal/state_clients/registry.go
└── utils/
```

---

## Consistency Models

| Model | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `ATOMIC` | Strong consistency - all replicas see same value |
| `CONVERGENT` | Eventually consistent - replicas converge |
| `CAUSAL` | Causal consistency - respects causality |
| `SEQUENTIAL` | Sequential consistency |
| `TOPIC` | Pub/sub topic (no persistence) |
| `QUEUE` | FIFO queue |
| `PRIORITY_QUEUE` | Priority queue |
| `LEADER_ELECTION` | Leader election primitive |

---

## Injected Proto Enums

After generation, each proto file gets:

```proto
enum TypeID {
  TYPE_ID_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  TYPE_ID_MESSAGE_1 = 1;
  TYPE_ID_MESSAGE_2 = 2;
  // ... one per message
}

enum RpcID {
  RPC_ID_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  RPC_ID_SERVICE_METHOD_1 = 1;
  // ... one per RPC method
}
```

---

## Files to Read

1. **Start here**: `TACPLUS_FINDINGS.md` (this directory)
2. **Quick visual**: `tacplus_summary.txt` (10 sections, visual format)
3. **Complete reference**: `tacplus_exploration.md` (656 lines, all details)
4. **Real example**: `/Users/jody/workspace/letsencrypt/tacplus/registry/registry.go` (2.2MB generated)

---

## Common Questions Answered

**Q: Where does the registry get generated?**
A: `types/registry.go` (root), `types/services/.../registry.go` (per-proto)

**Q: What metadata is available?**
A: Everything in TypeInfo, FieldInfo, BoundaryInfo protos - types, fields, constraints, boundaries, consistency models, persistence

**Q: How does tacplus know what to generate?**
A: Reads tacplus.yaml, scans proto files for service_state annotations, collects all types recursively

**Q: Is the registry per-service or global?**
A: Both! Root registry is global + per-service nodes for hierarchical access

**Q: Can I access nested type metadata?**
A: Yes! TypeInfo.Fields contain nested FieldInfo.Message with full descriptors (recursive)

**Q: What about validation constraints?**
A: All in FieldInfo.Constraints as strings describing rules

**Q: Can types be looked up by name?**
A: Yes! LookupType(fqn) or lookupByShortName() via maps (O(1) lookup)

---

**See TACPLUS_FINDINGS.md for detailed navigation and file locations**

```
8. Inject TypeID/RpcID enums
9. Generate service wrappers + HTTP clients
10. Run post-gen hooks
```

---

## 💡 Key Concepts

### Type Collection Algorithm
1. Build message/enum index from all proto files
2. For each message: create FQN, build TypeDescriptor recursively
3. For each field: collect type, constraints, nested descriptors
4. Marshal to JSON schema
5. Determine TypeDir (services vs libs)
6. Sort by FQN deterministically

### Consistency Models
- `ATOMIC`: Strong consistency
- `CONVERGENT`: Eventually consistent
- `CAUSAL`, `SEQUENTIAL`: Other models
- `TOPIC`, `QUEUE`, `PRIORITY_QUEUE`, `LEADER_ELECTION`: Special types

### TypeID/RpcID Enums
Automatically injected into proto files:
```proto
enum TypeID { TYPE_ID_MESSAGE_NAME = 1; ... }
enum RpcID { RPC_ID_SERVICE_METHOD = 1; ... }
```

```yaml
  - services/identity.IdentityState:rw
  - services/kernel.ServiceHealthState:rw
grpc-servers:
  - services/identity.IdentityService
```

# tacplus.yaml Reference

`tacplus.yaml` is the configuration file for tacplus code generation. Place it in your project root.

## Fields

| Key | Type | Description |
|-----|------|-------------|
| `language` | string | **Required.** `go`, `java`, `typescript`, `python`, `rust` |
| `output-dir` | string | **Required.** Output subdirectory relative to project dir |
| `src` | string | Proto source (git URL or local path). Defaults to the shared proto repo. |
| `pkg` | string | Canonical package name in Java-style reverse DNS (e.g., `com.gitlab.secondstarcavalier.controlplane.services.kernel`). Converted to native format per language. |
| `import` | string | Path to base config to import (resolved relative to this file) |
| `grpc-servers` | list | gRPC services to generate server wrappers for |
| `grpc-clients` | list | gRPC services to generate gRPC + REST client wrappers for |
| `rest-clients` | list | Services to generate REST client wrappers for. If omitted, follows `grpc-clients`. |
| `all-grpc-servers` | bool | Generate server wrappers for ALL gRPC services |
| `all-grpc-clients` | bool | Generate client wrappers (gRPC + REST) for ALL gRPC services |
| `all-rest-clients` | bool | Generate REST client wrappers for ALL gRPC services |
| `all-grpc` | bool | Shorthand for `all-grpc-servers` + `all-grpc-clients` |
| `states` | list | State roots with access mode (`:rw`, `:ro`, `:worm`) |
| `all-states` | bool | Import all state roots as read-only |
| `state-only` | bool | Generate only state infra, no gRPC lifecycle |
| `post-gen` | list | Commands to run after generation (`cmd` + `args`) |

## Entry Formats

### gRPC / REST Client Entries

Format: `path/file.ServiceName[.InstanceName]`

```yaml
grpc-clients:
  - services/baseball.BaseballService
  - services/football.FootballService.NFC    # with instance name
```

The `.proto` extension is optional — `services/baseball` resolves to `services/baseball.proto`.

### State Entries

Format: `path/file.MessageName:rw|ro|worm`

```yaml
states:
  - services/baseball.BaseballState:rw
  - services/football.FootballState:ro
```

Access modes:
- `:rw` — full read-write access (get, set, lock, delete)
- `:ro` — read-only access (get, watch)
- `:worm` — write-once read-many (get, set, add, publish, offer)

## REST Client Resolution

When `rest-clients` is **not set**, REST client generation follows `grpc-clients` / `all-grpc-clients`. This preserves backward compatibility — existing services with `grpc-clients` continue to get REST clients automatically.

When `rest-clients` **is set**, it controls REST client generation independently. This lets a service generate REST clients without also generating gRPC clients:

```yaml
# REST clients only — no gRPC client stubs
rest-clients:
  - services/baseball.BaseballService
```

```yaml
# gRPC clients for baseball, REST clients for football
grpc-clients:
  - services/baseball.BaseballService
rest-clients:
  - services/football.FootballService
```

`all-rest-clients: true` generates REST clients for every discovered gRPC service, regardless of `grpc-clients`.

## Generated Output Structure

Output directory depends on language:
- **Go / TypeScript / Python / Rust**: `tacplus/`
- **Java Maven**: `target/generated-sources/tacplus/`
- **Java Gradle**: `build/generated-sources/tacplus/`

Within the output directory:

```
tacplus/
  types/           # Proto message types
  sm/              # Service manager
    internal/
      grpc_clients/   # gRPC client wrappers
      rest_clients/   # REST client wrappers
      handler/        # Handler interface
  utils/            # Validation helpers, utilities
```

## Config Composition

Configs can import a base file and override specific fields:

```yaml
# tacplus-base.yaml
language: go
src: https://gitlab.com/org/proto.git
all-grpc: true

# tacplus.yaml
import: tacplus-base.yaml
grpc-servers:
  - services/baseball.BaseballService
rest-clients:
  - services/football.FootballService
```

Multiple config files can also be passed via CLI:

```bash
tacplus build -c tacplus-base.yaml -c tacplus-overrides.yaml
```

Later files override earlier ones. Merge rules:
- **Strings**: overlay wins if non-empty
- **Booleans**: `true` wins (cannot unset a boolean via overlay)
- **Lists**: overlay replaces entirely if non-empty

## Post-Generation Hooks

```yaml
post-gen:
  - cmd: go
    args: [run, ./cmd/bufgen]
  - cmd: npx
    args: [prettier, --write, tacplus/]
```

Commands run with the project directory as CWD after code generation completes.

## CLI Flag Equivalents

| YAML Key | CLI Flag |
|----------|----------|
| `grpc-servers` | `--grpc-server` |
| `grpc-clients` | `--grpc-client` |
| `rest-clients` | `--rest-client` |
| `all-grpc-servers` | `--all-grpc-servers` |
| `all-grpc-clients` | `--all-grpc-clients` |
| `all-rest-clients` | `--all-rest-clients` |
| `all-grpc` | `--all-grpc` |
| `states` | `--state` |
| `all-states` | `--all-states` |
| `src` | `--src` |

CLI flags override YAML values when both are specified.
